title: Structured Approach for Assessing Fall Risk
recommendation_text: Conduct a standardized fall risk assessment using the Timed Up and Go (TUG) test by asking the patient to rise from a chair, walk 10 feet, turn around, walk back, and sit down. Document the time taken and observe for unsteadiness. For patients taking >12 seconds or showing unsteadiness, implement a personalized fall prevention plan.
implementation_guidance: Perform assessment during routine visits for all patients 65+ or those with balance concerns. Use a standard chair (seat height 18 inches) and mark the 10-foot distance clearly. Document results in a dedicated fall risk section of the EHR.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 25% more patients at risk for falls, 30% reduction in fall incidents among identified high-risk patients, and decreased fall-related emergency department visits.
target_population: Adults 65+ and younger patients with neurological conditions, balance disorders, or multiple medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening (under $5 per patient) with potential for significant cost savings from prevented falls ($14,000+ per fall-related hospitalization).
citation_authors: Lusardi MM, Fritz S, Middleton A, et al.
citation_title: Determining Risk of Falls in Community Dwelling Older Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Using Posttest Probability

title: Specific Technique for Medication Reconciliation
recommendation_text: Ask patients to bring all medications (prescription, over-the-counter, supplements) to each visit in their original containers. Compare with the medication list in the EHR by asking: 1) 'How do you actually take this medication?' 2) 'Do you ever skip doses or take it differently than prescribed?' 3) 'Have you stopped taking any medications?' Document all discrepancies and update the medication list.
implementation_guidance: Send medication bag reminder before appointments. Allocate 5-10 minutes for reconciliation. Use a standardized documentation template. Flag high-risk medications (anticoagulants, insulin, opioids) for special attention.
expected_outcomes: Identification of medication discrepancies in 40-60% of patients, 25% reduction in adverse drug events, and improved accuracy of medication lists.
target_population: All patients on multiple medications, particularly during care transitions, older adults, and those with complex medication regimens
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential to reduce medication errors and related hospitalizations.
citation_authors: Mueller SK, Sponsler KC, Kripalani S, et al.
citation_title: Hospital-based medication reconciliation practices: a systematic review

title: Specific Questions for Assessing Medication Understanding
recommendation_text: For each new medication, ask patients these four questions: 1) 'What is the name of this medication?' 2) 'What is it for?' 3) 'How much do you take and when?' 4) 'What side effects should you watch for?' Document areas of misunderstanding and provide targeted education to address knowledge gaps.
implementation_guidance: Implement during medication counseling for all new prescriptions. Use plain language explanations for medical terms. Provide written information at appropriate literacy level. Document patient's understanding in the EHR.
expected_outcomes: Improved patient knowledge of medications by 40%, 30% reduction in medication errors, and increased patient confidence in medication self-management.
target_population: All patients receiving new medications, particularly those with limited health literacy, cognitive impairment, or complex medication regimens
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention requiring minimal additional time with potential for significant reduction in medication-related adverse events.
citation_authors: Marvanova M, Roumie CL, Eden SK, et al.
citation_title: Health literacy and medication understanding among hospitalized adults

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Inhaler Technique
recommendation_text: Ask patients to demonstrate how they use their inhaler with a placebo device. Observe for specific errors in technique: 1) Failure to exhale before inhalation 2) Improper seal around mouthpiece 3) Inadequate breath hold after inhalation 4) Incorrect timing of actuation. Provide immediate correction and re-demonstration until proper technique is achieved.
implementation_guidance: Assess technique at initial prescription and at least annually thereafter. Keep placebo inhalers for all commonly prescribed devices. Document specific errors observed and corrections provided in the EHR.
expected_outcomes: Identification of technique errors in 60-80% of patients, 25% improvement in symptom control after technique correction, and reduced emergency department visits for respiratory exacerbations.
target_population: All patients using inhaled medications, particularly those with asthma or COPD
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential to improve medication effectiveness and reduce acute care utilization.
citation_authors: Sanchis J, Gich I, Pedersen S, et al.
citation_title: Systematic Review of Errors in Inhaler Use: Has Patient Technique Improved Over Time?

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Vaccine Hesitancy
recommendation_text: Use the CASE approach when discussing vaccines: C (Corroborate) - acknowledge the patient's concerns; A (About me) - share your expertise and experience; S (Science) - explain the scientific evidence; E (Explain/Advise) - provide a clear recommendation. Document the specific concerns raised and your response.
implementation_guidance: Implement during preventive care visits or when vaccines are due. Avoid dismissing concerns or overwhelming with statistics. Use motivational interviewing techniques to explore barriers. Document the conversation and follow-up plan.
expected_outcomes: 15-20% increase in vaccine acceptance among hesitant patients, improved patient-provider trust, and increased overall vaccination rates.
target_population: Patients expressing vaccine hesitancy or refusing recommended vaccines
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant public health benefits and potential reduction in vaccine-preventable diseases.
citation_authors: Jacobson RM, St. Sauver JL, Finney Rutten LJ

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Suicidal Ideation
recommendation_text: Ask these three direct questions in sequence: 1) 'Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself in some way?' If yes, ask: 2) 'Have you had thoughts of how you might do this?' If yes, ask: 3) 'Have you had intentions to act on these thoughts?' Document responses verbatim and implement appropriate safety planning based on risk level.
implementation_guidance: Ask questions in a private setting. Maintain a calm, matter-of-fact tone. Have crisis resources immediately available. Document risk assessment, safety plan, and follow-up arrangements in the EHR.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 30% more patients with suicidal ideation, appropriate risk stratification, and reduced suicide attempts through timely intervention.
target_population: All patients with depression, substance use disorders, recent life crises, or previous suicide attempts
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening with potential for life-saving interventions and prevention of costly emergency services.
citation_authors: Posner K, Brown GK, Stanley B, et al.
citation_title: The Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale: initial validity and internal consistency findings from three multisite studies with adolescents and adults

title: Specific Approach for Medication Adherence Barriers
recommendation_text: Ask patients who are not taking medications as prescribed: 1) 'What makes it difficult to take your medication?' 2) 'What would make it easier?' 3) 'What have you tried that has helped?' Based on responses, implement targeted interventions such as dose simplification, reminder systems, or cost assistance.
implementation_guidance: Use a non-judgmental approach. Focus on practical solutions rather than emphasizing non-adherence. Document specific barriers identified and interventions implemented. Schedule follow-up to assess effectiveness.
expected_outcomes: Identification of specific adherence barriers in 80% of non-adherent patients, 25-30% improvement in medication adherence rates, and better disease control metrics.
target_population: Patients with chronic conditions requiring long-term medication therapy, particularly those with demonstrated non-adherence
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential to improve treatment effectiveness and reduce complications.
citation_title: Engaging Patients to Optimize Medication Adherence

title: Specific Technique for Pain Assessment in Non-verbal Patients
recommendation_text: Use the PAINAD (Pain Assessment in Advanced Dementia) scale to assess pain in non-verbal patients by observing: 1) Breathing 2) Negative vocalization 3) Facial expression 4) Body language 5) Consolability. Score each category from 0-2 and document total score (0-10). Implement pain management interventions for scores ≥4.
implementation_guidance: Assess during rest and with movement. Observe for at least 5 minutes. Compare scores over time to evaluate treatment effectiveness. Document scores and interventions in the EHR.
expected_outcomes: Improved pain detection in 40% of non-verbal patients, more appropriate analgesic administration, and reduced distress behaviors.
target_population: Non-verbal patients, particularly those with dementia, cognitive impairment, or communication disorders
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with potential for significant improvement in quality of life and reduction in distress behaviors.
citation_authors: Warden V, Hurley AC, Volicer L
citation_title: Development and psychometric evaluation of the Pain Assessment in Advanced Dementia (PAINAD) scale
citation_journal: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Health Literacy in Discharge Instructions
recommendation_text: Use the teach-back method for discharge instructions by saying: 'I want to make sure I explained your care plan clearly. Can you tell me in your own words: 1) What health problem you were treated for 2) What medications you need to take 3) What warning signs to watch for 4) When your follow-up appointment is?' Address any misunderstandings before discharge.
implementation_guidance: Implement for all discharges. Use plain language without medical jargon. Provide written instructions at 5th-6th grade reading level. Document use of teach-back and areas requiring clarification.
expected_outcomes: 30% reduction in post-discharge medication errors, 25% reduction in readmissions, and improved patient satisfaction with discharge process.
target_population: All patients being discharged from inpatient care, particularly those with limited health literacy, complex discharge plans, or high risk for readmission
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential to reduce costly readmissions and post-discharge complications.

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Alcohol Use
recommendation_text: Use the AUDIT-C three-question screening: 1) 'How often do you have a drink containing alcohol?' 2) 'How many drinks do you have on a typical day when you are drinking?' 3) 'How often do you have six or more drinks on one occasion?' Score each question 0-4 and implement brief intervention for scores ≥4 (men) or ≥3 (women).
implementation_guidance: Screen annually for all adult patients. Use a matter-of-fact, non-judgmental approach. For positive screens, conduct brief intervention using motivational interviewing techniques. Document scores and interventions in the EHR.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 20-30% more patients with unhealthy alcohol use, 15-20% reduction in alcohol consumption among those receiving brief intervention, and increased referrals to treatment.
target_population: All adult patients, with particular attention to those with conditions that may be exacerbated by alcohol use
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening with potential for significant reduction in alcohol-related health problems and healthcare utilization.
citation_authors: Bush K, Kivlahan DR, McDonell MB, et al.
citation_title: The AUDIT alcohol consumption questions (AUDIT-C): an effective brief screening test for problem drinking
